routing_warnings.description: The request to retain CAD files as part of a long-term documentation set belongs to the maintenance and product documentation Requirement.
The claim that CAD files and other records were saved concerns retention of the documentation set rather than completion or delivery of the system-layout artifact.
The freelancer's verification that the listed electrical and mechanical components are mutually compatible belongs to the separate component-interface compatibility Requirement.
The claim that the BOM and other records have been saved concerns retention of the documentation set rather than preparation of the BOM itself.
The request to retain a wiring layout as part of a broader long-term documentation set belongs primarily to the maintenance and product documentation Requirement.
The client changes the spout's physical pour direction; that independently testable orientation change belongs to the spout-orientation Requirement.
The concrete runtime observation is a plumbing leak, not a failure of pour-stream quality.
The freelancer's target-specific repair claim concerns the plumbing leak.
The explicit claim that the plumbing has no leaks belongs to leak prevention; the broad statement that everything will work does not specifically establish pour quality.
The spout-specific change in this message concerns removability for cleaning, not the rendered stainless-steel appearance.
This message changes the spouts’ downward pouring direction, which is independently represented by the spout-orientation Requirement.
The explicit implementation assurance in this message concerns removable whisks; its bowl-clearance statement remains provisional.
The proposed twist-lock attachment and need to remove the obstructing whisk primarily concern the independent whisk-removal Requirement.
The observed plumbing leak establishes a failure of leak-free plumbing but does not report liquid reaching electrical components.
The claimed plumbing repair addresses the leak-prevention Requirement without specifically establishing electrical isolation.
The cracked fitting explains the plumbing leak but provides no evidence of contact with electrical components.
The claim that the plumbing has no leaks supports leak prevention, not the distinct electrical-isolation Requirement.
The change to an 80A adapter and higher-power controllers concerns internal load capacity and overheating headroom rather than the external 120V wall-power decision.
Verification that the complete power system and mechanical interfaces are mutually compatible belongs to the component-interface compatibility Requirement.
The statement that startup and shutdown require plugging or unplugging the machine primarily establishes the missing user-operated power-switch behavior.
The proposed replacement of the current switch with a rendering-matched button concerns the power control's visual design rather than whether user-operated power switching is required.
The requested clarification concerns the appearance and proposed replacement style of the power button, not the functional power-switching behavior.
Lighting around the power button is decorative lighting evidence rather than a change to functional startup and shutdown control.
The verification that the complete power system and mechanical interfaces are mutually compatible primarily concerns component interface compatibility rather than electrical load capacity.
The reported plumbing leak is separate from the sturdiness claim and belongs to the leak-prevention Requirement.
The observed plumbing leak is a concrete failure of leak prevention, not evidence that sustained operation as a whole was tested.
The freelancer’s statement that the machine is sturdy is an implementation claim about structural stability.
The claim that the plumbing was fixed belongs to the leak-prevention Requirement.
The cracked fitting identifies the cause of the plumbing leak and supports the leak-prevention trajectory.
The claim that the repaired plumbing has no leaks belongs to the leak-prevention Requirement.
The client selects the smaller bowl size; this changes bowl capacity and geometry rather than the enclosure-size Requirement.
The client accepts the depicted bowl size; the separate beige finish belongs to REQ_MACHINE_COLOR_FINISH.
The client asks about the dimensions and resizability of the separate base section.
The reported 12.25-inch height and plumbing-based resizing constraint concern the separate support base.
In the immediately preceding platform discussion, the requested beige finish and font-color match apply to the newly proposed support base rather than clearly modifying the main machine enclosure.
The requested beige finish and font treatment concern the base's visual branding rather than its structural cup-clearance function.
The logo, uppercase lettering, and font change concern support-base branding.
Reproducing the reference rendering aesthetically concerns the base's visual design rather than its cup-clearance structure.
The request to place a cursive E on every button belongs to the dedicated button-markings Requirement.
The beige lettering specification applies to the dedicated button-markings Requirement.
The proposed E treatment is distinct from the general DJ-style control appearance.
The unresolved proposal to replace the current on-off switch concerns the power-control Requirement rather than decorative control styling.
The requested lighting around the power button belongs to the decorative-lighting Requirement.
The logo along the bottom belongs to the support-base branding Requirement.
The rendered color request belongs to the machine color-and-finish Requirement.
The freelancer's statement that the buttons can still be marked with E is specific to the dedicated button-markings Requirement.
This beige color instruction predates the separate support base and applies to the machine design.
This message changes the base logo, typography, and font rather than its physical color or finish.
The beige-finish clause changes the separate support-base finish Requirement rather than its graphics and typography.
The rendered buttons and Deck 1/Deck 2 labels concern control styling rather than support-base graphics.
Lighting around the power button belongs to the decorative-lighting Requirement.
The rendered-color clause concerns the support-base finish Requirement.
